articles.title: Fatigable weakness, ptosis and diplopia
articles.th: อ่อนแรงที่แย่ลงเมื่อใช้งาน หนังตาตก เห็นภาพซ้อน — นึกถึงโรครอยต่อเส้นประสาท-กล้ามเนื้อก่อน
body: Weakness that worsens with use and recovers with rest points to the neuromuscular junction. Look at the eyes first: asymmetric ptosis that drops further during sustained upgaze, variable diplopia and normal pupils make myasthenia gravis the leading diagnosis. Reflexes and sensation stay normal.

Three questions sort the mimics. Are the pupils involved? Dilated, sluggish pupils with descending paralysis suggest botulism. Are the legs and autonomic system affected more than the eyes? Think Lambert–Eaton, especially in a smoker. Is the ophthalmoplegia fixed and symmetric? Consider a mitochondrial or dystrophic myopathy, or restrictive thyroid eye disease (lid retraction rather than ptosis).

Bedside: sustained upgaze and the ice pack test. Laboratory: AChR, then MuSK/LRP4 antibodies; repetitive stimulation or single-fibre EMG; CT chest for thymoma. Monitor vital capacity whenever bulbar or neck weakness is present.

articles.title: Acute ascending or flaccid weakness
articles.th: แขนขาอ่อนแรงเฉียบพลันลามขึ้น รีเฟล็กซ์หาย — นึกถึง GBS แต่ต้องแยกไขสันหลัง รอยต่อประสาทกล้ามเนื้อ และเกลือแร่
body: Symmetric weakness that climbs from the legs over days, with lost reflexes and mild sensory symptoms after an infection, is Guillain–Barré syndrome until shown otherwise. The danger is respiratory and autonomic failure, so serial vital capacity matters more than oxygen saturation.

Before settling on GBS, look for a sensory level and early bladder failure (spinal cord), fatigable eye signs with normal reflexes (myasthenia), descending paralysis with fixed pupils (botulism) and low potassium (periodic paralysis). Pure motor disease after diarrhoea suggests the axonal form AMAN; early nerve studies can be misleading, and repeat studies separate reversible nodal block from true demyelination.
If the illness keeps progressing beyond 8 weeks, or relapses after treatment, reconsider acute-onset CIDP or an antibody-mediated nodopathy.

articles.title: Chronic demyelinating neuropathy and CIDP mimics
articles.th: เส้นประสาทเสื่อมแบบ demyelinating เรื้อรัง — แยก CIDP จากโรคที่เลียนแบบ เช่น nodopathy, anti-MAG, POEMS, MMN, CMT
body: CIDP weakens proximal and distal muscles over more than 8 weeks, with widespread areflexia and large-fibre sensory loss, and usually responds to IVIG, steroids or plasma exchange. Proximal weakness is the clue that separates it from length-dependent axonal neuropathies.

Many disorders imitate it. Ask: is there a paraprotein? IgM with anti-MAG gives a distal sensory-ataxic pattern with tremor; a lambda band with organomegaly, skin change and high VEGF means POEMS. Is the patient young with tremor, or older with nephrotic syndrome, and not responding to IVIG? Test for NF155 and contactin-1 antibodies. Is weakness asymmetric, purely motor and nerve-by-nerve? That is multifocal motor neuropathy. Lifelong, uniform slowing with pes cavus suggests Charcot–Marie–Tooth.
Every chronic demyelinating neuropathy deserves serum and urine immunofixation.

articles.title: Nodo-paranodopathies
articles.th: nodopathy คือโรคที่แอนติบอดีโจมตีบริเวณ node/paranode — คล้าย GBS/CIDP แต่รุนแรงและไม่ตอบสนอง IVIG
body: The node of Ranvier and its paranodal junctions hold the sodium channels and the glial–axonal seal that make saltatory conduction work. Antibodies against these structures produce conduction failure that can reverse quickly or progress to axon loss, which does not fit the old axonal-versus-demyelinating split.

Clinically these patients look like GBS or CIDP with atypical features: severe distal motor weakness, sensory ataxia, tremor (NF155), older age and nephrotic syndrome (contactin-1), neuropathic pain (Caspr1), or a catastrophic GBS-like illness with cranial and autonomic involvement (pan-neurofascin).

Most antibodies are IgG4, which does not activate complement — one reason IVIG often fails. Plasma exchange, steroids and especially early rituximab work better. Test for nodal antibodies when 'GBS' or 'CIDP' is unusually severe or IVIG-resistant.

articles.title: Neuropathy with a paraprotein
articles.th: เส้นประสาทเสื่อมร่วมกับโปรตีนโมโนโคลนอล — แยกชนิด IgM/IgG/IgA และหาโรคเม็ดเลือดที่ซ่อนอยู่
body: A monoclonal protein turns up in about one in ten people with an unexplained chronic neuropathy, and becomes commoner with age, so the link may be coincidental. The job is to decide whether the paraprotein is causing the neuropathy and whether a malignant clone lies behind it.

The pattern guides the search. IgM with a slow, distal, sensory-ataxic demyelinating neuropathy suggests anti-MAG (or Waldenström). IgG or IgA with a CIDP-like picture is treated much like CIDP. A painful small-fibre neuropathy with autonomic failure suggests AL amyloidosis. Painful mononeuritis multiplex with purpura suggests cryoglobulinaemia. A lambda band with a disabling motor neuropathy, organomegaly, skin changes and very high VEGF suggests POEMS.
Workup: immunofixation of serum and urine, free light chains, and haematology review (marrow, skeletal imaging), adding anti-MAG, VEGF, cryoglobulins or fat pad biopsy as the pattern suggests.

articles.title: Sudden focal deficit
articles.th: อาการทางระบบประสาทเฉพาะที่เกิดทันที — คิดถึง stroke ก่อน ตรวจน้ำตาลและ CT ทันที
body: A deficit that is maximal at onset and fits one arterial territory is vascular until proven otherwise. Time last known well, a glucose check and a non-contrast CT come first, because they decide reperfusion: CT separates haemorrhage from infarction, and CT angiography finds large-vessel occlusions suitable for thrombectomy.

The common mimics have tell-tale features: a witnessed seizure before the weakness (Todd's paralysis), positive spreading symptoms followed by headache (migraine aura), a low glucose (hypoglycaemia), and inconsistent weakness with a positive Hoover sign (functional disorder).
After the acute phase, the mechanism drives prevention: cardiac rhythm, carotid imaging, small vessel risk factors, and in young patients dissection or venous thrombosis.

articles.title: Thunderclap and worst-ever headache
articles.th: ปวดศีรษะรุนแรงทันทีภายในนาที — ต้องหาเลือดออกใต้เยื่อหุ้มสมองและสาเหตุอันตรายอื่นทุกครั้ง
body: A headache that reaches full intensity within a minute is a red flag regardless of how well the patient looks. Subarachnoid haemorrhage is the first concern: CT within 6 hours is very sensitive; later presentations need lumbar puncture for xanthochromia and vascular imaging.

If the CT and CSF are clear, think of reversible cerebral vasoconstriction (recurrent thunderclaps over days, triggers such as exertion or serotonergic drugs), cervical artery dissection (neck pain, Horner), cerebral venous thrombosis, and pituitary apoplexy (visual loss, ophthalmoplegia, low cortisol).

articles.title: Papilloedema and raised intracranial pressure
articles.th: จอประสาทตาบวมจากความดันในกะโหลกสูง — ต้องหาก้อน หลอดเลือดดำอุดตัน ก่อนวินิจฉัย IIH
body: Bilateral optic disc swelling with headache means raised pressure until proven otherwise. Imaging must exclude a mass and venous sinus thrombosis before a lumbar puncture measures the opening pressure.

Idiopathic intracranial hypertension is a diagnosis of exclusion, typically in women with recent weight gain; the outcome that matters is vision, so formal visual fields guide treatment. A sixth nerve palsy can appear without any lesion in the brainstem (false localising).

articles.title: Parkinsonism: idiopathic or atypical?
articles.th: พาร์กินสันแท้หรือชนิด atypical — ดูความไม่สมมาตร การล้มเร็ว การกลอกตา ระบบอัตโนมัติ และการตอบสนองต่อเลโวโดปา
body: Bradykinesia with decrement is the required feature; rest tremor and rigidity support it. Idiopathic Parkinson's disease starts on one side, stays asymmetric and responds clearly to levodopa.

Red flags change the diagnosis. Falls in the first year and slow vertical saccades suggest PSP. Early severe autonomic failure, cerebellar signs or stridor suggest MSA. Asymmetric apraxia and cortical sensory loss suggest corticobasal degeneration. Early fluctuating cognition with visual hallucinations suggests Lewy body dementia. Symmetric signs on dopamine-blocking drugs suggest drug-induced parkinsonism, and a magnetic gait with incontinence suggests normal pressure hydrocephalus.

articles.title: Tremor at the bedside
articles.th: แยกชนิดอาการสั่นจากสถานการณ์ที่เกิด: ขณะพัก ขณะยกค้าง หรือเมื่อเข้าใกล้เป้าหมาย
body: Classify tremor by when it appears. At rest, disappearing with movement: parkinsonian. With arms held out and during action, bilateral and often familial: essential tremor (check thyroid and drugs). Worsening as the finger approaches a target: cerebellar outflow, for example in multiple sclerosis. Jerky, position-specific tremor with abnormal posture: dystonic.
Tremor with neuropathy is a clue in its own right — anti-MAG and neurofascin-155 neuropathies both cause disabling action tremor.

articles.title: Cognitive decline: tempo tells the story
articles.th: สมองเสื่อม — ความเร็วของการดำเนินโรคช่วยแยกสาเหตุ หลายปี (AD) เป็นขั้น (หลอดเลือด) หรือภายในเดือน (CJD/autoimmune)
body: Years of insidious memory loss with failed cueing suggests Alzheimer's disease. Stepwise decline, slowed thinking and executive problems with white matter disease suggest vascular cognitive impairment, which often coexists with Alzheimer pathology. Early behavioural change points to frontotemporal dementia; fluctuations, hallucinations and REM sleep behaviour disorder to Lewy body dementia.

Decline over weeks to months is a different problem: look for treatable autoimmune encephalitis, infection, metabolic and nutritional causes before accepting prion disease. Lobar microbleeds in an older patient raise cerebral amyloid angiopathy.

articles.title: Acute vertigo: peripheral or central?
articles.th: เวียนศีรษะบ้านหมุน — แยกหูชั้นในกับก้านสมอง/สมองน้อยด้วยรูปแบบเวลาและการตรวจ HINTS
body: Ask about timing first. Seconds of spinning with head movement is BPPV — confirm with Dix–Hallpike and treat with repositioning. Continuous vertigo for days is an acute vestibular syndrome: vestibular neuritis or a posterior circulation stroke. Recurrent attacks of minutes to hours suggest vestibular migraine or Ménière's disease.

In the acute vestibular syndrome, HINTS helps: an abnormal head impulse, unidirectional nystagmus and no skew favour a peripheral cause; a normal head impulse, direction-changing nystagmus or skew deviation demand urgent imaging for stroke.

articles.title: Spinal cord syndromes
articles.th: อาการไขสันหลัง — ขาอ่อนแรงสองข้าง ชาถึงระดับหนึ่ง ปัสสาวะผิดปกติ ต้อง MRI ด่วนเพื่อหาการกดทับ
body: Weakness of both legs with a sensory level and bladder disturbance localises to the cord. The first priority is an urgent MRI of the whole spine to exclude compression from tumour, disc, abscess or haematoma.

Without compression, tempo and pattern guide the cause: hyperacute (infarction), days (inflammatory: MS, NMOSD, MOGAD, post-infectious), weeks to months with dorsal column loss and neuropathy (B12 or copper deficiency, nitrous oxide), or lightning pains with Argyll Robertson pupils (tabes dorsalis).

articles.title: Fever with headache or confusion
articles.th: ไข้ร่วมปวดศีรษะหรือสับสน — ให้ยาปฏิชีวนะและ acyclovir ก่อนรอผล ถ้าสงสัย
body: Fever, headache and neck stiffness suggest meningitis; fever with confusion, behavioural change or seizures suggests encephalitis. Do not wait for imaging or lumbar puncture to give empirical antibiotics, and add acyclovir when encephalitis is possible.

CSF patterns help: neutrophils with low glucose (bacterial), lymphocytes with very low glucose and very high protein (tuberculous or fungal), lymphocytes with normal glucose (viral or autoimmune). Subacute psychiatric change with seizures and dyskinesia in a young woman suggests anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.

articles.title: Seizures, status and their mimics
articles.th: ชัก — แยกจากเป็นลมและ dissociative seizure; ชักเกิน 5 นาทีถือเป็น status ต้องรักษาทันที
body: A convulsion lasting more than five minutes, or repeated seizures without recovery, is status epilepticus: check glucose, give a benzodiazepine, then a second-line agent, and search for the cause.

For a single event, the witness account decides. Reflex syncope has a prodrome and quick recovery even if a few jerks occur. Dissociative seizures are often long, with eyes closed and fluctuating movements. Morning jerks in a teenager suggest juvenile myoclonic epilepsy; an epigastric rising sensation and automatisms suggest temporal lobe epilepsy.

articles.title: Upper versus lower motor neuron signs
articles.th: แยกรอยโรค UMN กับ LMN — ถ้าพบทั้งสองแบบในแขนขาเดียวกันโดยไม่มีอาการชา นึกถึง ALS
body: Upper motor neuron lesions give spasticity, brisk reflexes, clonus, Hoffmann and Babinski signs, with weakness in a pyramidal pattern. Lower motor neuron lesions give wasting, fasciculations, low tone and reduced reflexes.

The combination matters. UMN and LMN signs together in the same region without sensory loss suggest ALS; absent ankle jerks with extensor plantars suggest combined cord and nerve disease such as B12 deficiency. Pure LMN weakness following individual nerves, with conduction block, suggests multifocal motor neuropathy, a treatable mimic of ALS.

articles.title: Proximal weakness: muscle or something else?
articles.th: อ่อนแรงต้นแขนต้นขา — แยกกล้ามเนื้ออักเสบ กล้ามเนื้อเสื่อม และโรครอยต่อประสาทกล้ามเนื้อ
body: Difficulty rising from a chair or lifting the arms with preserved reflexes and sensation suggests a myopathy. Weeks of symmetric weakness with a rash means dermatomyositis; an older patient with finger flexor and quadriceps weakness has inclusion body myositis; asymmetric scapular winging with facial weakness suggests FSHD; myotonia with distal weakness and cataract suggests myotonic dystrophy.

Do not forget the junction: Lambert–Eaton causes proximal leg weakness with autonomic symptoms, and myasthenia can present with neck and shoulder weakness. CK, EMG, myositis antibodies, muscle MRI and targeted genetics sort most cases.
